C-PROGRAM-DELIVERY-DASHBOARD.Summary: Make Projects the bilingual AICC Program Backlog and delivery Kanban, register the existing service-resolution proposal in the Portfolio Funnel, and connect Initiative goals to their native project documents and governed delivery items.
C-PROGRAM-DELIVERY-DASHBOARD.Problem: The Projects front lists an unregistered proposed Initiative while the Portfolio shows only maintained Registry items. Readers cannot follow its goal through Portfolio intake and delivery. Projects has no Program Kanban even though the delivery model defines one; the maintained Program Backlog currently has no admitted Capabilities or Features.

Goals.Goal: Render /en/projects/ and /ru/projects/ as a compact Program Backlog with Delivery board, Portfolio intake and Project documents views, using maintained Registry state.

Register the existing service-resolution proposal as one ordinary Proposed Initiative, currently INI-013 subject to identifier recheck, in PRI-1, with its existing outcome hypothesis and a six-section incomplete Initiative Brief.

Connect Portfolio Initiative, native project document bundle and recorded Solution/Capability/Feature relationships through stable identities and reciprocal links, without duplicate maintained statuses or authoritative records.

Support actual delivery review through state/stage, rank, acceptance criteria, responsible roles, dependencies, next decisions, dates and shared capacity, retaining the complete native project workbook.

Constraints.Constraint: The Program Kanban follows Solution Lifecycle Model 4.2 and 5.1: Backlog, Ready, Active, Review and Done, with Urgent, High priority and Normal service classes. Completed pending review remains in Active; Waiting retains its underlying column and Dependency; Accepted and Closed remain distinct; parked and other off-flow exits remain inspectable.

Ordinary Capabilities enter after the recorded MVP continue decision under Portfolio Management Model 7.2 and Solution Lifecycle Model 3.1. Run-rate Features enter directly under Approved Standing Initiatives through the recorded Weekly Review admission. Proposed workbook steps are not admitted Program items; do not invent CAP, FEAT, SOL, DEP, AGR or DR identifiers to populate the board.

Read delivery identity, hierarchy, rank, service class, state/stage and admission/acceptance evidence from the Program Backlog; Initiative state and goals from Portfolio Backlog and Briefs; capacity from board.md; observations from the Dashboard; dependencies from the existing Dependency records. Validate contradictions and invalid parents. Extend maintained bilingual fields only where a governed field lacks a place, without a second tracker.

Feature in-progress capacity remains one shared place across ordinary and run-rate work, including Active, Completed, Review and Waiting after start; Ready Features remain limited to two. Capability in-progress and Ready limits remain one each. Ordinary Initiative MVP/Implementation capacity remains shared at one, excluding Standing Initiatives. Derive limits rather than inventing allocations.

The new Initiative remains Proposed/Funnel, unranked and unscored. Its expected Tier 2 is not assigned or cleared. Keep unknown requester/appointments, selected journey, baselines, targets, time-box, estimates, project-specific dependencies, approval and acceptance unknown. Recording intake does not approve the business case, take it into Discovery, issue an agreement, start an MVP or admit delivery work.

Reconcile only the bounded intake records in both Registry editions: new Initiative Brief and Portfolio Backlog entry, Portfolio board, Dashboard counts and Program introduction. Use actual registration date explicitly as Funnel entry, leaving original proposal date unknown. Preserve all earlier decisions, six existing ranks, PI observations, dates and limits. Distinguish the intake update from the last Weekly Review baseline.

The Registry owns the lean Initiative Brief and proposal identity. The native project charter displays Registry-derived identity/state and a Portfolio summary link; retain its complete authored business-case draft and measurement annex as supporting working material. Correct its present claim to display the maintained Registry record, obsolete registration placeholders and relationship references only; preserve remaining authored content, all twelve documents per language, diagram labels/geometry, tables, local destinations and diagram controls.
DR-2026-061 notices apply only to Initiatives actually covered by that goal confirmation. No old approval, goal decision or reported achievement is inherited by the new proposal.

Keep published progress role-safe: no personal names, Bank financial figures, data, code or closed evidence bodies. Unknown flow observations are not zero; dates are used only for their recorded meaning.

Use common AICC fonts, compact neutral cards, magenta rules and tapered wrapping selection accents; provide equivalent EN/RU views, both themes, responsive reading, keyboard controls, direct links, no-script content and portable output.

The user's requested Initiative/project relationship permits explicit reciprocal Portfolio/Projects body links. Keep each section's content ownership and search scope, existing routes and common navigation. Do not broadly import neighbouring content or alter charter rules.

The interface reads, filters and reveals maintained progress. It does not persist approvals, edits or state changes in browser storage, introduce a backend, perform Jira cutover or replace the separate Program Board or Team Work Item board.

After approval and passing verification, complete approved durable reconciliation and archive, preserve concurrent work, commit and push clean source, publish through the maintained deployment tool, and verify the served manifest and actual bilingual relationships.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Approving the service-resolution business case, choosing its journey, funding, staffing, dates or risk assignment, starting its MVP, admitting delivery items, or changing existing business decisions and ranks.
Changing charter admission/acceptance rules, constructing a sample operational backlog, introducing a duplicate record store, shared editor, new governance cadence or authenticated integration.
Rewriting unrelated project wording, Discovery or Lab content, replacing the Program dependency/iteration board or Team board, or refreshing on-demand portable exports.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: After bounded registration, Portfolio shows seven ordinary Initiatives: one Proposed in Funnel and the six existing Discovery: Scoping records in Reviewing; four Approved Standing Initiatives remain separate. Original ranks, decisions and shared limits remain unchanged.

The maintained Program Backlog has zero recorded Capabilities and Features at this baseline, and the delivery board reports zero items accurately. Capacity is Features 0/1 in progress and 0/2 Ready, Capabilities 0/1 in progress and 0/1 Ready. No project plan step appears as an approved or active delivery card.

The new project card, Portfolio card, intake view and project overview share one Initiative identifier, goal and state. Readers can follow Portfolio to the complete project workbook and back, and every existing Initiative has an intake or Standing admission-source relationship with actual delivery eligibility.

The native project charter links to the maintained Initiative summary and shows its actual identity/state, retaining the full supporting business-case draft and measurement annex; its source-of-truth claim and obsolete unregistered-identifier wording are corrected in both editions without unrelated content loss. All existing project documents, tables, diagrams, native interaction paths and destinations remain available.

Fixtures independently verify nonempty delivery projection, ordinary versus run-rate parent admission, state/stage mapping, Waiting dependency context and capacity, Completed versus Accepted/Closed, ranked order, unknown measurements, and fail-closed contradictory records. The empty real baseline is checked separately from synthetic fixture data.

EN/RU desktop/intermediate/mobile and light/dark views retain common typography, contrast and no page overflow. Tab/filter/disclosure interactions, keyboard focus, scoped search, counterpart routes, no-script reading and temporary direct-file output work.

Unit checks, complete-site idempotent build/link checks, bounded relationship checks, record-to-view checks and relevant browser consumer paths pass; GRACE ownership and verification match the approved source changes.
Clean committed source is published; served manifest and live Portfolio/Projects show the verified Registry baseline and reciprocal project relationship.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Maintained Registry consistency and translation freshness; exact intake and empty delivery baseline; synthetic nonempty parent/admission/state/capacity boundary fixtures; full retained workbook comparison allowing only approved source-of-truth/registration substitutions; accessible bilingual themed consumer paths, portable export and served release verification.

Assumptions.Assumption: The user asks for an operational delivery view and bounded registration of the supplied proposal, not business approval. The user approved the concrete design and completed build plan on 2026-10-06 with “push and publish”; this includes implementation, verified apply/archive, commit, push and publication.

The next available Initiative identifier is currently INI-013 and will be rechecked before writing. The date of actual entry is a new intake observation, not proof of an earlier proposal or Weekly Review.
